Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

give thanks verb

also say grace, saying grace, giving thanks, thank, thank you for (doing something), thank you for helping me, thanks for your gifts, thank you for

classical

Traupman 393
Caes. BG 1.41: decima legiō … grātiās ēgit, quod dē sē optimum jūdicium fēcisset (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 109: grātiās agō quod (+ indicative)

grātiās agere

give thanks, say grace

+ dative of the person; prō + ablative of the thing. grātiās agere is thanking in words; grātiam referre is repaying in deed (Cic. Off. I 47).

Examples

  • Pater caelestis, ā quō omne dōnum perfectum dēscendit, grātiās tibi agimus prō hōc cibō … et prō hāc domō

    Heavenly Father, from whom every perfect gift comes down, we thank you for this food … and for this homecomposed

  • Ego grātiās agō.

    I say thank you.composed

  • Cōnfitēminī Dominō, quoniam bonus: quoniam in aeternum misericordia ejus.

    Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endures for ever (said responsively, Dad the first half-verse and Theo the second).Ps. 135 [136], 1

  • Grātiās tibi agō quod mē jūvistī.

    Thank you for helping me.Traupman 109

  • grātiās tibi dē dōnīs tuīs: sed tū mihi ea servā

    thanks to you for your gifts: but keep them safe for meAug. Conf. 1.20.31

  • Grātiās tibi dē dōnīs tuīs.

    Thanks for your gifts.Traupman 393

See also thank you, Thanksgiving Day, fold one’s hands, the Lord’s Prayer.

SourcesLewis & Short: gratia

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 109, 393.
